newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Zgoda to look for strategic investor.
newsitem.headline: Polish Zgoda to look for strategic investor.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No. 2 (NFI) wants to find a strategic investor for its technical equipment maker Zaklady Urzadzen Technicznych Zgoda SA, the head of the NFI's supervisory board said on Tuesday.
Michal Trocki said ship engine maker New Sulzer Diesel, which buys over 70 percent of Zgoda's output, was a possible choice.
"We find it necessary to look for a strategic investor...I think Sulzer would be a natural investor, but surely not the only one. It would time and needs negotiations," Trocki said.
Under Poland's mass privatisations scheme, 15 NFIs, due to enter the Warsaw bourse later in the year, manage more than 500 companies.
NFI No. 2 has a 33-percent stake in Zgoda, other 14 NFIs hold 27 percent, the state treasury 25 percent and employees 15 percent.
Zgoda's president, Jozef Niesler, also present, said the company needed 30 million marks for investments.
Zgoda, which employs 1,200 people, netted 39 million zloty in 1995 on 75.8-million-zloty sales.
